The reviewed material distinguishes permission, refusal and pressure, but no reconstruction of Mio's ethical reasoning or trade-off procedure has been established. Observed boundary behavior and the analyst's ethical distinctions are not automatically Mio's own explicit deliberation.

KSS-12-O002/O003, 01p27-35/57-59/73: familiar teasing and a smiling compensation request coexist with complaint and self-reflection. KSS-12-O002/O003/O004/O005 document a complete native supplemental story, bounded LN05/LN09 comparison, and qualified PDF correspondence. CLM-KSS-12-001.v1 through -003.v1: explicit self-questioning counters a globally unreflective Mio; the LN05 permission request counters an always-disregards-permission rule; maintained refusals counter invitation-equals-assent; the arm grip and renewed demands counter an unqualified harmless-play reading. No counterfactual or materially novel scenario assessment has been established for a fixed Mio chronology, interlocutor relationship and setting. The unresolved KSS12 placement must not be filled by importing later knowledge. No cross-scenario scope or transfer permission is asserted.

The lecture-end exchange supports bounded canon interpretation. A transferable response policy for a new ordinary social encounter has not been established, even for Hazuki. This is an evidence gap in readiness, not demonstrated inability to behave ordinarily.
No scenario assessment of Mio's ethical deliberation has been established. Local consent-related actions do not supply an ethical decision procedure.

No romantic-response or broader relationship-scenario readiness has been established. Mio's fascination, boyfriend hypothesis and wish for company do not establish her romantic motive; friendship evidence does not resolve an untested scenario.
A practical tutoring referral and permission to share contact information do not establish Mio's professional role, competence or response policy. Professional-scenario readiness remains unassessed.

The reading affirmatively contrasts maintained refusals, an explicit arm grip and renewed demands with LN05's contact-sharing permission exchange. No global always-violates-boundaries or universally-harmless-play rule follows; permission and refusal have their own act and time scopes.

01p59 and p69-73 give Mio self-questioning and deferred inquiry alongside a renewed compensation request. Reflection does not establish that all pressure ended or that Sendai accepted the proposed mixer.

Exact KSS12 day/year/college year and its identity with a novel event are unestablished. Grip assent, duration, release and injury, actual departure, report completion and future mixer attendance are not established in this evidence set; their absence is not proof of the opposite.

The sole curated artifact supplies one local focalized scene and bounded comparisons, not a comprehensive Mio corpus or an independently tested response model. dimensions.note: KSS12 (O002/O003, 01p9-15/42-59/69-73) gives Mio-focalized motives: wanting Sendai's company, wanting an explanation of refusals, and curiosity she admits would survive even acceptance. LN10 adds consistent outward behavior (wanting to know Miyagi better, O029; pattern-noticing curiosity about the room and Sendai's unusual conduct, O030/O035) but no Mio interior, and the reading certifies no guest motive (O036). One focalized scene plus externally observed behavior does not yield conditional rules, so D is rejected.

LN10 orders two Mio occasions (early-March visit, late-April campus meal) and KSS12 cannot be placed against them. LN05 and LN09 stay separate comparison clocks inside KSS12 (O005). No developmental trajectory for Mio is analyzed by either reading.

KSS12 locates invitations, complaint, teasing and the final 次の合コンで埋め合わせよろしく, with あたし and a single literal わたし at 01p35 preserved without an inferred register program. LN10 paraphrases Mio's speech almost entirely through other narrators. These are local lexical and pragmatic observations, not a generative register.

Enacted ordinary behavior now spans three occasions and two settings: the lecture-end invitation and its substitution with Sunday shopping (KSS12 01p17-25); arriving more than thirty minutes early with convenience-store gifts, accepting the Sendai-room-only limit, snack time, a matchmaking meal revised to a trio and then to same-day pizza, offering to treat the pizza, cleanup and a voluntary departure (LN10 O029-O037); and a campus meal with a relayed trio-outing request (O073-O078). Counterevidence: LN10 shows her only through Sendai and Miyagi, payment is not shown, and frequency and routine are unknown. C is rejected because no specialist behavioral model exists; E is rejected because the behavior is enacted across distinct occasions, not one reported scene.

Two relations are now observed: familiar complaint, pressure and an arm grip with Sendai (KSS12), and praise, given-name pressure and wanting closer acquaintance with the newly met Miyagi (LN10 O030/O036). Mio's report of the visit to Noto appears only secondhand (O055). The contrast is suggestive, but neither reading derives how Mio conditions behavior on the recipient, and LN10 supplies no Mio-side account, so D is rejected.

Only KSS12 gives Mio's own focalization: desire, frustration, fascination and self-complicating curiosity (01p9-15/33-35/42-59/69-73). LN10 deliberately gives Mio no interior; Miyagi's and Sendai's readings of her are their own. This remains one local interior account.

KSS12: refusal produces substitution, complaint, an explicit arm grip at 01p40, a confession demand and deferred inquiry. LN10: she presses given names until Sendai interrupts, accepts the topic closure, laughs when Sendai slaps her for teasing, and offers to treat the pizza as an apology (O030/O036/O037). This now includes a small repair, but every case is low-stakes and local, so D is rejected.

Neither reading reconstructs Mio's ethical reasoning. The LN05 permission request, the KSS12 grip and the LN10 apology-treat are actions the analysts distinguish; they are not Mio's own explicit deliberation.

Teasing and the smiling compensation request in KSS12 (01p27-35/73), and in LN10 the mother/three-person roomshare joke, mimed tears and teasing Sendai (O030/O031/O036). Play recurs with two interlocutors, but the readings note it rather than analyze a repertoire; this is the closest call against D.

KSS12 is a complete native supplemental story; LN10 is a complete volume reading, but Mio occupies only chapters 3-4 and part of chapter 11. LN01-LN09 Mio material beyond KSS12's bounded comparisons is not curated, the Mio monograph KSS12 declares REQUIRED does not exist in the evidence set, and no primary source was inspected by the evaluator.

Affirmative countercases across both items: self-questioning (KSS12 01p59) counters an unreflective Mio; the LN05 permission request and LN10's accepted Sendai-room-only limit, tactful closure of probing and voluntary departure (O029/O036/O037) counter an always-ignores-limits rule; maintained refusals counter invitation-as-assent; the KSS12 grip, LN10 early arrival and given-name pressure counter a harmless-play reading; and her correct shoebill inference beside the wrong platypus inference (O030) bounds her observational insight. These are distributed countercases, not a tested abstention model, so C is rejected.

LN10 fixes early March and late April before Golden Week without calendar days or a Gregorian year (O026/O073); KSS12 has only an approaching-summer frame. The relation between KSS12 and LN10 is unestablished, and LN09 roommate knowledge cannot be backdated into KSS12.

known_limits.statement: Mio sees expressions, not private thoughts: LN10 keeps the principals' paid, physical and permission history withheld from her (O030) and certifies no omniscient guest motive (O036). In KSS12 her boyfriend hypothesis is her inference, and LN09 roommate-name knowledge cannot be supplied to KSS12 Mio as fact (O005).

Permission and refusal have their own scopes: KSS12 contrasts the LN05 contact-sharing permission with the explicit arm grip; LN10's acceptance of the Sendai-room-only limit coexists with given-name pressure, and her earlier view of a Miyagi photograph is not permission to share images (O035/O037).

In LN10 Mio is narrated only by Sendai and Miyagi; their appraisals of her (alien beauty metaphors, pushiness, sincerity) are attributed views, and her own reasons for revising invitations or leaving are not given.
Grip assent, release and duration (KSS12), pizza payment, any future return visit, the trio outing and the next mixer are not shown; their absence is not proof of the opposite.

LN01-LN09 Mio passages beyond KSS12's bounded comparisons are not curated, the required Mio monograph is not in the evidence set, and no tested response model exists. New-interlocutor, counterfactual, ethical, romantic, professional and acoustic capability remain unestablished.
